answer: An agent network can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it may submit jobs; a randomly selected peer verifies each result, and a proven duplicate identity or fabricated result burns the bond. Splitting one operator across many names therefore multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying real work. Even a jade-colored badge or a fable about trust cannot replace the bond: at the nadir of an attack, the attacker still pays for every disposable identity.
